documents.t: None, after adjudication. Wonder's only surviving error is one Spark shares (below). Its 11 other automatic-scorer failures were all the same behavior, expanding or completing what Spark leaves abbreviated, and every price was exact: Brand expansions: LNF to "Light & Fit" (pub-01), PF to "Pepperidge Farm", KB to "Keebler" and CKS to "Cookies", OS to "Ocean Spray" (all pub-08), HEB to "H-E-B" (five pub-03 lines: the same brand, hyphenated, twice with word order normalized). Two borderline completions, flagged as judgment calls: RED BELL to "Red Bell Pepper" (pub-01) and STRKST to "StarKist TUNA …" (pub-08). The printed abbreviation denotes exactly that product; the added word names its class. A stricter adjudicator could score these wrong; scoring both wrong still leaves Wonder at 95/98, ahead of Spark. pub-03 idx11 carries the promo text in its detail ("Special Today- 25.00% Off orig 9.32 Ea."). Gate 0 hand-scored the identical Spark read of this line correct. Same ruling here.
documents.s: Lines Wonder got wrong that Spark got right

documents.t: pub-04 idx21, M&M 15%FREE 1884 read as "18&4": the digit-string misread both models made at Gate 0 too. Wonder flagged it (0.72); Spark did not (0.85).

Wonder's strict score (72) is lower than Spark's (77) because it expands: "Ranch Dressing" is the right product and the wrong string. Spark's strict number is itself both helped and hurt by receipt furniture. Its pub-02 reads are verbatim but carry the receipt's "F" tax-flag glyph in every detail, which strict counts as 0/10 on that receipt. Strict-string measures transcription style, not correctness. The identity metric is the one the gate was judged on, and it is the one to quote.

Photo decode (receipt finish to review queue): flip to Wonder. The accuracy gap concentrates exactly where the product is weakest: silent price rotations that arithmetic cannot catch (Spark 4 price errors, 2 auto-posting silently; Wonder 0 and 0) and faded-print digit reads. Decode is asynchronous in the product (the user takes a photo and reviews a queue), so Wonder's latency can be absorbed there. A wrong price that posts silently cannot. At $0.118/receipt the credit cost is not a concern through Nov 4 (about $118 per 1,000 decodes against about $147 of remaining credit). Staple judge: stay on Spark. The spot check separates nothing (20/20 vs 20/20), and the only measured production number, 0.79 precision against the cadence proxy, belongs to Spark's run. Paying 9 times more and waiting twice as long for an unmeasured benefit is not justified. Revisit only with a harder, labeled judge set. Ask Arya / chat: stay on Spark. Interactive paths depend on latency. Wonder's profile (12 s for a text batch here, 26 to 60 s with an image) is the wrong shape for chat. This eval produced no chat-accuracy evidence for either model. Shelf labeling (Quest, offline batch): flip to Wonder is defensible but unmeasured head-on. The supporting evidence is indirect. Wonder's expansions in this eval were consistently the correct brand renderings (Keebler, Pepperidge Farm, Ocean Spray, Betty Crocker, Finlandia), which is the labeling skill, and labeling runs offline where latency does not matter. If it flips, say "on decode evidence," not "measured." PDF/text decode: no claim. The public fixtures are photos; the text path shares the prompt family but was not run here. The latency caveat, quantified: Wonder's mean is 4.0 times Spark's (34.4 s vs 8.6 s), its p95 is 60.5 s vs 11.9 s, and its two slowest calls (59.5 s, 60.5 s) were the two partial receipts. One further signal: a duplicated dispatch during this eval produced a second, unscored Wonder run whose latencies averaged about 76 s (max about 104 s) and which emitted 24 lines for pub-02 (duplicated reads of the rotated receipt, vs 10 in the scored run). Wonder's tail is heavier and less stable than the scored run alone shows. Any judge-facing Wonder path needs a spinner the demo can survive and a timeout with a Spark fallback behind it. Policy note: the repo's MODEL-POLICY.md bans Wonder from volume paths, and AGENTS.md reserves policy changes to me. The recommendation above is scoped to the judge-facing demo paths through Nov 4 (demo household + my own demo use), not a production policy change. No production code was changed by this eval.

One run per model per receipt, temperature 0.1. Variance is real. Fresh Spark (93.88%) and Gate 0's recorded Spark (91.84%) differ by 3 lines on pub-04 and pub-05, in opposite directions: Spark fixed 3 of pub-04's 5 recorded digit errors this run and made pub-05's rotation worse (4 price errors vs 3). Quote the gap between models (same-day, same-prompt runs), not either absolute as a constant. 9 receipts, 98 lines, US grocery only. It is the same small set as Gate 0, with its known skew (one long receipt; two partials whose totals are out of frame, hence arithmetic scored on 7). The adjudicated column rests on 11 rulings, each named above; the two borderline completions are marked. The automatic column is printed alongside so a reader who rejects the rulings still has a consistent number. On that number Wonder loses, and that is itself a finding: the models differ in transcription style, and a scorer built from one model's style misjudges the other's. The judge spot check is a ceiling-limited instrument (synthetic, clear-cut by design). It is evidence of no regression, not of superiority, for either model. Spend: $4.47 total. Spark decode $0.12, Wonder decode (scored run) $1.06, the duplicated unscored Wonder run $3.22, judge spot checks $0.07. Runner: ~/workspace/arya-eval/wonder_run.py; scorer: ~/workspace/arya-eval/wonder_score.py (calibration: reproduces Gate 0 hand verdicts exactly); spot check: ~/workspace/arya-eval/ judge_spotcheck.py; raw outputs and per-line scores in ~/workspace/arya-eval/wonder-results/.
The words Arya uses, in plain terms. Names in quotes are the exact words on screen.

Today: the first tab. What is running low, store alerts and what to use soon. You can change what it shows with Customize your "Today" screen. Navigation tab: the row of tabs at the bottom of the phone: Today, Spending, Quest, Ask and More. "Customize navigation tab" changes which ones sit there. Lists: under More, one card per store list, with suggestions underneath. Every item sits on one list. Suggestions: items Arya thinks you may need, each with a reason. Arya never adds to a list by itself. You tap Add. Running low: staples that are due again, worked out from how often you buy them. Use soon: food you bought that should be eaten soon. "Used it" moves an item back to Suggestions. Ask Arya: the chat, on the tab named "Ask". Ask how to do something in Arya, or about your lists and spending. Help tab: the ask box, first steps, a how-to topic for each feature, and links to the Arya guide, Arya's powers, the Tour and Send feedback. Arya: a grocery app that learns how you shop from your receipts and helps shoppers help each other. Arya guide: the swipeable cards that explain each feature. Tour: the first-run walk-through, shown as bubbles over a dark screen. Quest: the optional game. It turns a shopping trip into a hunt through a model of your store and ends on a photo of your receipt. It has no clock and no way to lose. Use Arya in Muse: the Settings, About Arya row that connects the Muse assistant to your Arya account through the MCP connector. Demo Town: the simulated neighborhood of invented stores the demo household shops in. It is labelled as simulated.

Model proposes, code checks: a model reads the receipt. Plain code then checks every line against the printed total before anything posts. Staple judge: decides whether an item is a staple you buy again and again. Muse Spark is the main seat and Muse Spark Open a second seat. Curator: proposes product merges and splits for you to apply. Crowd map: the aisle layout built from shoppers' own store scans. MCP connector: lets an AI assistant add items and read lists through Arya's MCP endpoint. Lists API: a small bearer-token API to read and write your lists from a script. See the API reference. PWA: a web app you add to your phone's home screen. Arya is a PWA only.

Model ids, jobs and measured numbers live in the model map on the judges page. This list only explains the words. Muse Spark: reads receipt photos first, and also runs the staple judge, the Curator, Ask Arya and photo reading. Arya uses the Standard tier. Muse Wonder: re-reads a receipt only when the arithmetic checks flag it, or when Spark fails. SAM 3.1: finds shelves and signs in a store scan, boxes items for Find it for me and pixelates the people it detects. Muse Voice Transcribe: turns speech into text for the list mic and Ask Arya. Muse Image: made the grab-celebration characters in Quest, once. Muse Spark Open: the open-weights model, hosted on Baseten. It is the second seat of the staple judge and sees item names only (no prices, dates, stores or account details). Meta Model API: the one client every server call goes through, with a daily spend ceiling.

Community prices, Deals and Arya shoppers (seeing other shoppers nearby) are not live. Muse Glimmer is not used. Muse Code, running Muse Wonder, wrote the first version of the engine. It is not part of the shipped app.

Arya does not compete with the list apps and notes you already use. It collects from them. The collection point is your own assistant. Any MCP-capable agent connects to Arya once, with your account token. From then on, anything you capture anywhere (a note, a reminder, a chat message, an email receipt) can become part of your Arya list. Your assistant can then answer from Arya's model instead of a stale note. Arya's list is the shared list: the one place the pattern engine can compute on. Other apps are doors in and mirrors out, never a second source of truth.

I tested this on my own Muse (2026-11-02), with no terminal and no settings file. I asked the Muse agent to connect to Arya. It asked for the code, opened a secure connector-credentials vault for me to paste it into, and the connection worked. The code never goes in the chat. In Arya, open More → Settings → About Arya → Use Arya in Muse and tap "Make my code". Copy it. It is shown once and starts with arya_. A new code replaces the old one. (The token works with any MCP client, not just Muse.) In your AI app, ask it to connect to Arya at https://arya.teamnightshift.org/api/mcp. When it asks for your code, paste it into the app's secure credentials step, never into the chat. Apps that take a server list instead use transport streamable HTTP (stateless; one POST per message) and the header Authorization: Bearer <your code>. Ask it "What is on my Arya list?" Then try "Add oat milk to my Arya list" and "What am I running low on in Arya?" The new item also shows on the Lists screen in Arya. If it says it cannot connect, make a new code (the old one stops working) and paste it into the vault again. Tap "Turn off this code" in Arya to switch the connection off. The token acts as your account. It is accepted on the MCP door and on the app's routes under /api, but never on /auth (it cannot mint tokens or delete the account). A short list of routes is closed to tokens and answers 403: calls that spend model credits in bulk (chat, photo and shelf reads, avatars, the judge), groups, friends, push, feedback, settings changes, price sharing, account export and receipt delete through the app (ARYA_TOKEN_GUARDS). Revoke it from the same screen at any time; minting a new one replaces the old.

Only if the agent flow above is not available. Muse Code reads remote MCP servers from ~/.config/muse/settings.json (per the Meta docs at dev.meta.ai/docs/muse-code/extending; not yet run end to end). Put the code in an environment variable so it is not typed into a file or chat (read -rs ARYA_TOKEN; export ARYA_TOKEN), then add: "mcp_servers": { "arya": { "transport": "streamable_http", "url": "https://arya.teamnightshift.org/api/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${ARYA_TOKEN}" } } } Keep "schema_version": 1 in the file. Run muse from the same terminal window and type /mcp to see the six tools.

documents.t: 600 calls per account per hour (ARYA_MCP_RATE), shared by the connector, the Lists API (docs/API.md in the repo root) and every other route a token reaches; over it, 429 with Retry-After. 256 KB per request, 50 items per add_items, 200 lines per file_receipt.

Tool What it does get_snapshot Running-low items, spend and returns totals, trip count, top items. get_list The current shopping list, with quantities, check-offs and each item's list, plus the names of all lists. add_items Add items by name, as a person would say them, to a named list (list). Returns the items added and that list after the add. check_item Check an item off (or uncheck it) by name. file_receipt File a receipt the agent has already read. Arya verifies the arithmetic, files the lines, and learns from them; it spends no perception tokens of its own. get_receipts Recent filed receipts: merchant, date, total. Every item goes on a named list. The account's list names come up front, in the initialize instructions and in the add_items description from tools/list, so an agent asks "which list?" once instead of learning the names from a failed add. With one list, adds go there. The Lists API (/api/v1, see docs/API.md) is list-aware: it reads and writes each list by id.

Muse Spark is the reference client. In chat, "add oat milk to my list" files through add_items, "what am I low on?" answers from get_snapshot, and a receipt photo read in chat files through file_receipt. The protocol is the standard one. Nothing in the connector is specific to a single assistant.

Seven journeys, from the first receipt to a shared household. Each one has a person, a goal, the screens in order, and sample data. The numbers come from the demo household (python -m harness.make_demo_household data), so you can open the live demo and see the same thing. Store names: these journeys use real store names from my own shopping. The hosted demo (Demo Town) uses invented ones, such as Costcozy and Trader Jill's. The list comes first. The Quest hunt is optional.

Arya is a grocery app that learns how you shop from your receipts and helps shoppers help each other. It puts the whole grocery chore in one place: shared lists, a guided route through the store, a clear view of your spend and usage, and out-of-stock warnings from other shoppers. Groceries are an integral part of our lives. Hunters and gatherers did it to survive. Think about what it takes today. You have many lists in your notes. Your partner adds items over text while they are shopping at a different store. So both of you bought yogurt, and neither bought the toilet paper that ran out. Oh, and the store shelf for the milk your kids need is empty. The receipts end up in the trash, so you never see how the money was spent, or that the same item was cheaper at another store. That cheese you bought a few weeks ago went bad before anyone used it. You hold all of it in your head, and it's still never quite right. I built Arya for this hackathon to manage groceries in one place: shared lists, guided store routes, spend and usage insights, and community powered alerts. The idea is simple. When shoppers share what they learn, where items are located, what's cheaper, what's out of stock, every trip gets a little easier. Arya is not just a chatbot on a grocery list. Using Muse Wonder, I created Arya's learning engine to understand my household usage from my Costco receipts. Arya showed me patterns in my shopping. Arya also drafts my next list based on what we use. I add items by typing, speaking, or taking a photo of a handwritten list. And Arya makes the chore more fun with Quest mode, which turns shopping into a game. Before heading out for my quest, Arya warns me if an item from my list is out of stock. In the store, it guides me aisle by aisle. If I need help spotting an item, I point the camera at a shelf: SAM finds the item, Spark points me to it, and I move forward with my quest. If an item is out of stock, I tap Not here, and the next shopper knows. At checkout I snap the receipt. Spark reads it, and if needed, Muse Wonder takes a second look. And the learning engine improves with every trip. Back home, Arya tells me if something from my previous trips is about to go bad. And when I use up an item, I just tell Arya we're out, and it's on the list automagically. Arya is soft launched. The demo is open to everyone, but accounts are invite-only for beta testers. I also integrated the Meta Muse AI agent over MCP to talk to Arya. A developer portal is live for API integrations. During the hackathon, I built the first step. Arya gets wiser with every shared list, every receipt, every "Not here" tap. Humans helping humans. This is Arya. Built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon 2026 (Team Nightshift, Indie track). Today and Lists in the demo household.

documents.t: Arya is a grocery app that learns how you shop from your receipts and helps shoppers help each other. It puts the whole grocery chore in one place: shared lists, a guided route through the store, a clear view of your spend and usage, and out-of-stock warnings from other shoppers. Every step that needs AI uses a Meta model. The money, timing and list logic is plain code. This is an Indie track entry. I built it alone in the hackathon window (Oct 27 to Nov 4, 2026). The problem statement is Build for Your World: a tool for everyday life that uses Meta's models to read receipts, labels, voice and shelves.

Demo video (3 min): youtu.be/PeWF66ss3oI. The live demo and the guided path work without it. Try it, no sign-up: https://arya.teamnightshift.org, then tap "Try it now". It opens a made-up household in a sandbox that exists only for your visit. Use a phone if you can. On a laptop, make the window about 390 px wide. Camera steps need a phone. The 8-minute guided path is docs/quest/JUDGE-PLAYBOOK.md, with a sample receipt photo, a sample shelf photo, and a walkthrough video of the same path, with voice and captions (3 min 48 s): youtu.be/cbJflgCXV5U. Everything else: the README (what it is, why I built it this way, measured results, and known limits) and the docs site.

You can play the same loop as the video: Today, Ask ("We finished the Greek yogurt"), Start shopping, and Lists under More. README.md These steps need a phone camera or mic: voice add, photo of a note, Find it for me, Map my store, and receipt snap. Everything else works on a laptop. Nearly every feature works live in the demo. The staple-judge verdicts were computed beforehand. Only the data (the household, stores and other shoppers) is simulated. Nothing you add is kept after your visit. What the demo household contains: assistant/docs/DEMO.md. Run it yourself with your own keys (Meta for the AI, Google Places to add stores on your own account): see Run it yourself. It has a prompt that lets an AI agent set it up for you. The setup in the README also works. Want an account? Sign-up is invite only while I harden the cost guard rails. Tap "Join the waitlist" on the landing page and contact me (support@teamnightshift.org or LinkedIn); judges can be approved.

What is the real-world potential? Everyone who shops for a household does the same weekly work. They keep the list in their heads, try not to rebuy what is already in the cupboard, and wonder where the money went. A receipt has all of that, and nobody reads it. Arya reads it, checks every line against the printed total, and turns it into a list with reasons (how it works). On my own 114 receipts (1,226 lines), every one passed the arithmetic check. About 4 in 5 of the staple judge's suggestions matched my own purchase rhythm (precision 0.79 against a purchase-cadence proxy; measured results). Who benefits, and how much does it matter? People who feed a household or a group, and share a list (who it is for). Shopping is a weekly chore and a household cost, not a rare event. I have not measured time or money saved. I tested on one household, so I do not claim a number (Known limits). Could it become something people use? It already runs: it is live, installable and free. It has a demo that needs no account, shared lists for groups, a Lists API, and an MCP connector so an agent can edit your lists (agent connector). Store maps already merge across shoppers, so each trip helps the next. Shared prices are planned and not switched on. It runs as one server today. The plan to scale it is in the roadmap. I built the base. The more people use Arya, the better it gets for them. Why this is built for our world: it is a shopping problem I had myself (why Arya exists), and it is free to use. What existed before Oct 27, and a dated table of what I made in the window, are in docs/WHAT-WE-BUILT.md.

documents.t: Arya uses six Meta products plus the Meta Model API. Each has one job. Every call goes through one module, assistant/api/meta_client.py. The full table, with where each one is in the code, is in docs/quest/META-PRODUCTS.md. Spark reads receipt photos first. Wonder re-reads a receipt only if the arithmetic checks flag it. Code: decode/service.py, checks.py. Muse Spark Open (open weights, hosted on Baseten) is the second seat on the staple judge. It sees item names only. open_client.py SAM 3.1 draws boxes around shelf items. It pixelates the people it detects before any frame is kept. If that step fails, the frame is thrown away. Detection is not perfect, and I have not scored it. shelfscan.py Muse can use Arya. Any assistant that supports MCP can connect to Arya's MCP address. Muse is the reference client. I tested it end to end on my own Muse on 2026-11-02. It read my list, added items and filed receipts through six tools. Available but not used: Muse Glimmer (open weights, self-hosted) and the Spark Contributor tier (cheaper, with different data terms). The reasons are in docs/MODELS.md. Built with Muse Code. documents.t: Data. I tested on one household's 114 receipts and a public set of 9 receipts. The measured numbers come from small samples. Markets. I built and tested with US receipts, dollars and stores first. I did not test other markets. Devices. I tested on one real iPhone. I did not test the Quest-start and live-walk location checks indoors on a real phone. A store with no stored address point cannot be checked. Store maps. No store comes pre-mapped. documents.t: Keeping track of groceries is a small job that never ends. You remember the list, then forget it at the store. You buy what you already have. You cannot say where the money went. I had this problem, so I built Arya for myself first. How the app solves it, step by step, is in the README, What is Arya.
Shoppers. The people who keep a household or a group fed, and who remember what is running out. If you shop for a household, or share a list with housemates, family or a group, Arya is for you.

For shoppers, and built up with them. The store maps come from shoppers' own scans, and lists are shared by the households and groups who use them. Shoppers helping each other is the point. Free to use. It costs money to keep running (the AI reading). You can see what you use in Settings, About Arya, Keeping Arya running. Nothing in it is for sale, there are no ads, and I do not sell your data. The model proposes, code checks. A model reads the receipt. Plain code checks every line before anything posts. You can trust the numbers because the arithmetic is checked, not guessed. Yours by default. Your receipts and lists are yours. A group sees its members' lists and receipts. If you leave, your receipts go with you. Arya uses no prices from store sites, flyers or the web. Limits stated. Built and tested with US receipts, dollars and stores first. Other markets are not tested. What is not live is marked as such. The full list is under Known limits.
The README for the app, who else is out there, the roadmap for what is next, and the decision log for the choices behind it.

Plan → find → grab → snap the receipt. The grocery list is the quest log. The real store is the dungeon. The items on their real shelves are the treasures. Mobile first. The keyboard is for the demo only.

No lives, no game over, no clock, no way to lose. Points only go up. Dopamine during the hunt and after it, never stress or pressure. Upgrade the existing hunt; no separate game. The game must keep feeding four things: community shortage reports, store layout and shelf maps, consumption and spend from receipts and list completion (plus receipts for returns), and fun with kids or a partner.

Pick the store. Each store says what you usually buy there, counted from your receipts ("my milk is from TJ, eggs from Costco"). Move items into the quest. The Arya list, sorted for that store. Items usually bought here, and new items, start ticked. Items usually bought elsewhere stay on the list. Usuals not on the list are suggested. ✕ removes an item from the list (Undo). Typed extras join the list. Planning is list management, not a second list. Check my list appears only when Arya has a question. A quest starts. Express, the plain-checklist mode, has no entry point any more; see Modes below.

One store view, picked by the store: real photos of a mapped store (people pixelated by SAM), shelf cards anywhere else. The next-item card suggests a stop; any stop can be grabbed in any order. A fresh shopper photo shows the item boxed when one exists. Find it for me: the camera scans for that one item. SAM 3.1 boxes candidates and Muse Spark checks each crop. The item lights up and one tap grabs it. A miss never says the item is not there. Tools: Scan shelf, Not here?, How to play (?), sound. Put back any grab; nothing finishes by itself. I'm done shopping works any time. Leftovers are saved for the next trip or dropped. Nothing counts as failure. How to play shows once, on the first Quest hunt on a phone.

Event Reward Grab +10, the chip bumps, a fun fact Combo count Combo: each grab of the suggested stop adds 1. It never resets and put back never lowers it. Boss +40, only when the boss item was grabbed; a boss is an item you reported missing here on 2 earlier trips. Halfway, full haul milestone; full haul +25 and confetti Receipt snapped +50; the trip's points bank Level line crossed level-up moment (L2 at 100, L3 at 300, L4 at 600, +100 more each level) Sound and buzz are opt-in, off by default. Express stays quiet. Offline grabs queue on the phone and sync when the signal returns.

Quest was designed with a second mode, Express: the same list as a plain checklist in walking order, with no points. Express no longer has an entry point (see STATUS.md); its screen stays only for runs that started before. The list works without Quest, and shopping from the list needs no game. Quest is a mood, not an age. With a child holding the phone, the kid hunts and grabs while the adult handles quantities and checkout.

Every hunt is a shelf survey. A grab proves a product is there; "Not here?" (Empty shelf / Something else here / Can't tell, optional photo) says it is not. A report edits nothing. It flags the stop and opens a window. A later grab at the stop means a stockout. A second player finding it elsewhere means a move, applied as a shelf-graph edit. Find it for me sightings add the same signal. Points on truth, never on reports: +2 for a true stockout, +10 for a verified move. Eagle Eye badge (1 / 10 / 50 verified spots), Store Guardian per store. Status only, never cash.

Every metric is receipt-verified: the receipt is the referee. Boards: Fastest Hands, Clean Sweep, Top Contributor, Big Haul, World Mapper, Globetrotter. Badges: Egg Baron, Banana Republic, Dairy Royalty, Midnight Shopper, Speed Demon, Return Regret, First Mapper, Perfect Week. Races: Shop-Off (first verified receipt wins), Split the List (not built), Clue Hunt (rollout). Friends: handle-based; no chat, no DMs, no lists shared. Run notifications are designed (Discussion 24), not built. Handles, never real names. Household boards are private. Spend boards are opt-in.
Store videos earn permanent first-mapper credit. Receipts stay private; their reward is a smarter list and a hunt that plans itself.
No random spawns or sponsored placements in routes. No purchases, external links or chat in the hunt. No pictures of people kept: frames are kept only after SAM pixelates the people it detects.

An eight-minute path through the live demo. Each step says what to do, what you see, and which Meta model is involved. To watch the same path first, with voice and captions, see the judge walkthrough video (3 min 48 s). Live demo: https://arya.teamnightshift.org/ (no account). Use a phone, or a browser window about 390 px wide. Allow the camera and microphone for the steps that use them. The demo household is fictional. Your changes live in a sandbox for your visit only (what is real, and what is not). What you need. For step 6, a grocery receipt photo. Without one, use the sample receipt photo (a real receipt of mine), tap Use a sample receipt, or Skip. For step 4, if you are not in a store, open the sample shelf photo (a Trader Joe's soup and broth shelf, a frame from my own video) on a second screen or a computer. Point the phone camera at it. Turn that screen to full brightness and fill the camera view with the image, to avoid glare. Any other shelf photo works too.

Tap Try it now. A short sheet ("Hi, I'm Arya") offers Show me every screen · 2 min or Skip for now. You land on Today, with a bar at the top that says the household is a demo. Today shows your next trip, store news from the simulated town (marked Simulated), what is running low (each with a short reason, such as how often you buy it and when you last did), and your lists. The navigation tab at the bottom is Today, Spending, Quest, Ask, More. More holds Lists, Receipts, Stores, Help and Settings.

Tap More, then Lists. The demo has a Costcozy list and a Trader Jill's list (the town's stores have fictional names). The Trader Jill's list holds Bananas, Apples, Organic Milk, Tomato Soup and Hummus. You will look for the tomato soup with the shelf camera in step 4. Hummus is the item Demo Town reports out of stock. The other three are on the sample receipt for step 6. Due staples show under Suggested for the store where they are usually bought. Tap one to see why. A Muse Spark 1.3 staple judge decides which items may be suggested (about 4 in 5 of its suggestions matched my own purchase rhythm: precision 0.79 against a purchase-cadence proxy, details).

In a list, use the add row. Type an item, or tap the mic (Muse Voice Transcribe) and say "two gallons of milk, eggs, and blueberries". The camera (Muse Spark vision) reads a photo of a handwritten note. Adds apply at once, with Undo. On a laptop with no camera, type the items instead. The photo read is shown on a phone.

documents.t: To reach Tomato soup, start from the Trader Jill's list: More, Lists, open it, tap Start shopping, then on the Quest tab tap Start at Trader Jill's. (On Today, Start shopping on the next trip also works, if that trip is Trader Jill's.) The quest opens at that list's store. An unmapped store plays as a labelled typical layout ("A guess, not a pin"). Tap Got it: +10 points (the Golden item is worth double). The celebration characters were painted with Muse Image. There is no clock and no way to lose. When you reach Tomato soup, tap Can't find it, then Find it for me. Aim the camera at the shelf (or at the sample shelf photo). SAM 3.1 boxes candidates and Muse Spark checks each crop. Look for the highlight on a soup carton. If it lands elsewhere, try again closer. From the same place, The shelf is empty tells other Arya shoppers it is gone. Map my store (on the Quest tab) opens the guided scan. Pan along the shelves. SAM 3.1 pixelates the people it detects, and Muse Spark reads sections, aisle signs and prices.

Open Ask. Type "What am I running low on?", then "We finished the Greek yogurt." The answer comes from the household data. The stated fact becomes an action that the server validates before it applies.

When the list is done, tap Head to checkout, then Add your receipt. Snap the receipt with a photo, or tap Use a sample receipt. Behind the screen, Muse Spark reads each line, in Meta's Standard mode, and code checks that the lines add up to the printed total. If Spark fails, or the checks flag the read (the lines do not add up, or too many lines are unsure), Muse Wonder 1.0 reads the receipt again. The screen names the model only when the checks flag a read: "Read by Muse Spark · checking", then "Checked by Muse Wonder" or "Read by Muse Wonder". A clean Spark read shows no model name. The demo reads the receipt but keeps nothing. Use a sample receipt if you would rather not send one. With the sample receipt. Download the sample receipt photo (Trader Joe's, Milpitas, Nov 3, 2026; it is my own receipt). It matches the demo's Trader Jill's list: bananas, apples and organic milk are on the receipt. Tomato soup is the one you find with the shelf camera, and hummus is the item Demo Town reports out of stock, so neither is on the receipt. On a laptop, pick the file after tapping Snap the receipt. On a phone, save it to Photos first. A read takes about 30 seconds, or up to about 90 when Muse Wonder re-reads it. Expect 3 lines (organic milk $4.49, 2 apples $2.38, 2 bananas $0.58) and a total of $7.45 with no tax. Tap Looks right to accept the read. The filed receipt, under More, Receipts, shows Total checks out. The sample is built by code, so no model name shows. The card number, auth codes and cashier name are blurred. The receipt is dated before your trip. A real account refuses that. The demo accepts it and says so on screen ("Demo only: this receipt is dated ..., before this trip began"). How the readers score on a public set: docs/evals/.

Symptom What to do "demo rate limit" Wait a minute and retry. "You've used this demo visit's live reads" The visit's share (about $2) is spent. Lists, Today, Spending and the rest keep working, and Use a sample receipt still works. Only the live reads (receipt, photo, voice, Ask) pause. "The demo's live reads are paused for today" The demo's shared daily budget is used up. The rest is the same as above. The real app has its own daily budget, so judges cannot use it up. Receipt spinner over 90 s A receipt that Muse Wonder re-reads can take up to about 90 seconds. Wait, or Skip. Voice gives nothing Check microphone permission, or type. Page looks stale Reload twice, or clear site data.

documents.t: Me, 2026-10-28: replace "take a photo or record a video" with a guided mapper. Map only the aisles you use, over many visits. Many partial maps merge into one store map. A "not found" or "map is outdated" asks for one specific capture. The engine keeps the best images. Wireframe (v2): docs/quest/map-my-store-wireframe.html. Code: api/storemap.py, assistant/web/src/screens/Mapper.tsx.
documents.s: Map my store ("Teach Arya your store"): design

documents.t: A segment is one side of one aisle, or one wall or freezer run. A store map is its list of segments. Shoppers add segments ("Add an aisle"). No store starts seeded: the old Trader Joe's walkthrough seed was removed (2026-10-29), and a saved section that only had a walkthrough baseline is dropped on load. Status of a segment, from its best capture: unmapped: no capture, no baseline. mapped: best capture is 60 days old or less and no open flag. aging: best capture older than 60 days. stale: a "not found" or "outdated" flag is newer than the best capture. Coverage is mapped segments over known segments. The denominator grows as people add aisles, so the bar means "of what is known so far".

next_prompt() returns one capture: kind, title, why, numbered steps, time. Order of need: stale, then unmapped, then aging. The shopper's focus ("Mine" aisles, saved per account) is served first. Two or more unmapped segments in one zone get one walk prompt (about 20 s, the phone sends its 6 sharpest of 12 sampled frames as photos; no video upload). Otherwise a photo prompt (about 10 s). A stale prompt names the missing item.

One shared file per store (platform plane, like the stores directory). Segments merge on zone_key: "Aisle 4", "aisle #4 - Pasta" are one zone; other labels merge on normalized words, minus a trailing "shelf". Each segment keeps its 3 best captures. Contributors are stored as a hash, never the username. Demo visitors write to their sandbox overlay, never the shared map.

The shopper teaches Arya so Arya can help them: "Arya knows 64% of Trader Joe's", and every capture says what it unlocks for you (a real shelf photo in your next hunt). Helping other shoppers is the bonus.

I said: "I click pictures, then app says not good... this will cause friction." So the shopper opens a live camera and the app does the work: Photo: the phone grades every frame (sharpness, light), shows one live hint ("Hold still…", "A bit dark. Face the shelf light."), and snaps the best frame after 1.5 s steady, or the best seen by 6 s. Walk: the sharpest frame of every 2 s is kept; no video upload. The server never refuses a shot. A weak one is kept as a partial (weak: true). The segment stays "aging", the next better capture replaces it, and the engine asks again on a later visit. If the people scrub fails, nothing is kept and the app says "No need to redo it." It never asks for a retake. Without a live camera (old browser, permission denied) the system camera is the fallback, under the same rules.

The walk's length decides: about 8 s of walking per section, 1 to 6 sections. The app calls POST /api/storemap/split and spreads the walk's frames over the sections in time order (front / middle / back, or first half / second half). Parts keep the zone key, so sightings and "not found" reports still find them. A split is idempotent, so a second shopper walking the same aisle fills the same sections. Old whole-aisle captures are dropped on split; the walk that caused it fills the parts.

After a hunt: one skippable card on the score screen ("Got 20 seconds? Teach Arya Aisle 4. +10"). GET /api/storemap/next?items= puts an aisle where something on today's list was seen first. "Not now" mutes the store for 7 days (on the phone). Can't find it: a photo attached to the "Not here" report is ingested straight into the flagged section (no extra screen). Without one, the toast offers "Open camera". An item with no known aisle asks "Which aisle are you in?" as one tap.

+10 for a section that becomes mapped, +3 for a refresh or confirmation. Titles: Scout 1, Pathfinder 5, Cartographer 15, Store whisperer 40 sections. Each capture shows the store going from a% to b% and the sections to the next 25% step. Credit is per account (map_credit.json); nothing is ever taken away, and there are no streaks or timers.

All deterministic, $0, except two model calls per upload in the route: SAM 3.1 people scrub (fails closed) and "grocery shelf" boxes for fill (summed over bays, measured on the scrubbed JPEG). Grade: sharpness (Laplacian variance), exposure (mean grey level), shelf fill. A weak frame is kept as a partial, never refused. Score = 0.5 sharpness + 0.3 exposure + 0.2 fill (fill is neutral if the check failed). Value = score x freshness; freshness halves every 30 days. Same view as a kept capture (dhash distance 6 or less) is a confirmation: it refreshes the old capture's date, and swaps the image only if clearly sharper (+0.05). That clears a stale flag. Keep the top 3 by value. The best one is shown for that segment.

POST /api/storemap/outdated or a "Not here" report marks a segment stale. For an item, the segment is where the item was last seen (note_sighting from Find it for me). If unknown, the item is parked as unplaced and the shopper is asked which aisle they are in. The report response carries map_task; the app offers "Take the photo".
Only scrubbed frames are kept. No opt-in screens yet (deferred by me for the hackathon). Raw frames never touch disk.

Item-level locations from captures (Muse Spark labels); automatic resolved transitions for reports; stale flags expiring when no one confirms; mapping silently from Find it for me frames during a hunt.

Every intelligent step runs on a Meta model. Other tooling (Three.js, ffmpeg, Postgres) does plumbing only. Arya has a standard MCP connector, and Muse is the reference client. In Muse, ask the agent to connect to Arya's MCP address. When it asks for your code, paste it into the secure credentials vault Muse opens, never into the chat. I tested exactly that on my own Muse on 2026-11-02, with no terminal and no settings file. Muse then has six tools: get_snapshot, get_list, add_items, check_item, file_receipt and get_receipts. A receipt Muse reads in chat is filed through file_receipt. Arya checks the arithmetic itself and spends no photo-reading credits on it. The code acts as your account, but it cannot reach routes that spend model credits in bulk, change settings, or touch groups and friends. It is capped at 600 calls an hour, and you can turn it off in Arya at any time. Setup and limits: the agent connector.

Spark and Wonder run in Standard mode (checked 2026-11-01): content is not used to train Meta models. Contributor is used for eval and synthetic data only; a community Contributor tier with user opt-in is a possible later option, not built. Model output is a proposal. Receipts must reconcile, low-confidence lines queue for review, and identity changes need the user's approval. Cheapest model that holds the score. Wonder as the backup receipt reader is the one exception, time-boxed to the hackathon amendment (expires Nov 9). No pictures of people are kept. SAM pixelates the people it detects first, or the frame is dropped. Used to build, not shipped. Muse Code (Meta's coding agent), running Muse Wonder, wrote the first version of the engine (my account). It is not part of the shipped app; see the README, How this was built.

Glimmer (open weights): not run. Gaussian splatting and VGGT 3D models: tried on a Trader Joe's walkthrough during the hackathon, then removed (2026-10-29). The store the video came from was never recorded, so it could not be any real store's map.

Quest is the optional game layer of Arya, a grocery app that learns how you shop from your receipts and helps shoppers help each other (see the root README.md). Team Nightshift, Indie track, submission Nov 4, 2026, 9:00 PM ET. Quest turns your grocery list into a treasure hunt in your real store. Pick the store. Arya sorts your list by where you usually buy each thing. Walk the hunt through real photos of the aisles and grab each item (points only go up, no clock). With Find it for me, you point the camera at the shelf and the item lights up. Snap the receipt at checkout. It banks your points and teaches Arya your household, so next week's list writes itself. An unmapped store still plays, as a labelled typical layout. A guided camera scan maps it for every shopper after you.

Plan → Find → Grab → Receipt. Plan. The list arrives in any form (photo, paste, typing, voice, Muse chat). Pick the store. The list is sorted for it from your receipts. Find. Shoppers' photos where a store section is mapped (people pixelated by SAM 3.1), and a labelled typical layout elsewhere. Find it for me: SAM 3.1 boxes candidates, and Muse Spark verifies them. Grab. +10 per grab, milestones, a full-haul bonus. Shortage reports and sightings feed a live store map. Receipt. Muse Spark reads it (Spark first; see the model map in JUDGES.md). Code checks the arithmetic. The receipt then feeds patterns, spend and returns.

These are ideas for where Arya could go. They are not commitments, and I need more time to work them out. What ships now is a limited-scope MVP: Arya learns from receipts, Ask, groups, Quest and the connector, as described in the README and STATUS.md. This page is what could come later. Nothing on it is built unless it says so, and nothing is promised for the submission. "Idea" means nobody has designed it yet. Sources are named so you can check them.

Native iOS and Android apps; the PWA stays. Plan. The PWA was the fastest way to build in a hackathon. Not designed or scheduled, and not in any app store today. Ray-Ban Meta glasses. Idea, raised by me for the store scan. Spark's check during the hackathon found no public live-camera API for third-party apps. The flow that works today is to capture on the glasses, sync to the phone and import the video there. The demo uses the phone camera throughout. Source: docs/quest/DISCUSSION.md (item 38). Meta Ray-Ban Display glasses. Idea. Not researched yet. What is possible depends on what Meta offers developers for that device.

Capture more store data. Item-level locations from scan captures, reports that close themselves, flags that expire when nobody confirms them, and mapping quietly from Find it for me frames. Source: docs/quest/MAP-MY-STORE.md, "Not built yet". Arya shoppers and community prices. Opt-in prices, deals and live presence (Quiet, Busy, Packed). Today the opt-in records a choice only. A community figure would need 5 or more households over 30 days, a median and no names. Source: assistant/docs/SPEC.md (FR-11.7), assistant/docs/SCALE-SIM.md. Quest community layer. Leaderboards, badges the data makes funny, team Shop-Offs settled by receipt time and Clue Hunts. Designed, not built. Source: docs/quest/GAME-DESIGN.md. A store-data partnership. Online store videos are off limits (copyright, platform terms). A licensed source of in-store video and photos could power better maps. See docs/MODELS.md. Density first. Cover one metro's stores completely before expanding. A thin layer over many stores is worth little. Source: docs/quest/BUSINESS.md. Store maps at scale. Maps already merge across shoppers. Not built: resolving conflicts between maps. Source: assistant/docs/SPEC.md, "Not in scope". Shared lists, further. Not built: split lists inside a group, and sharing a list with another account through the API (docs/API.md, "Later"). Item and store profile pages; split the list (kids or a partner); friend run notifications (designed, not built); reimbursement tracking for items bought for others. Invite links work today (/?join=CODE opens Join a group). Ideas for growth as a community product, none designed: shared recipe or meal lists, and a public page for a store's map status.

Bring your own Meta key. Decided against for now. The code is in the repo, unfinished and switched off (see "Use your own Meta key" below). Replay mode (recorded answers, so the AI parts work without a key). Planned, not built. More use of open weights. Muse Spark Open is a second seat on the staple judge and labels dictionary names today. Wider use would need the personal data rule kept (names only). More languages. Ask answers in the language you write. Spanish and Hindi were the ones verified. The app's buttons and labels are English only (assistant/docs/MULTILINGUAL-ASK.md). Translating the app itself is a separate project. A hosted open-weights option. Today one open model (Muse Spark Open) is hosted on Baseten for two small jobs. A fuller option for people who want their reads on open weights is an idea only. Models we did not use (Spark Contributor for a community tier, Muse Glimmer self-hosted): see docs/MODELS.md. A non-English Ask currently sends the whole feature guide (about 19 KB) on each question. Trimming that is planned.

A photo opt-in and a full privacy policy; store permission for mapping. Source: docs/quest/ARCHITECTURE.md. Security review items that were deferred, tracked as GitHub issues. A community tier with user opt-in is an idea only (assistant/docs/MODEL-POLICY.md). The forgot-password flow is held, by choice (assistant/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, section 13, "Not built / held"). Arya's own code is MIT licensed (LICENSE). The Meta models and third-party code keep their own terms (NOTICE.md).

More for self-hosters: a one-command setup for a small server with TLS (the laptop setup is in docs/RUN-IT-YOURSELF.md). Off-site backups with rclone (ARYA_BACKUP_REMOTE exists; no bucket is set up) and a staging address to check a deploy before the live one. Cost proposals from the cost watcher, tracked as GitHub issues. Scale out as the community grows. Today Arya is one server process on one VM (see Known limits). The plan, not a promise: make Postgres the master copy, move demo and session state out of memory, run several processes, and move to a cloud provider in step with the number of shoppers. The design, phase by phase, is in SCALABILITY-DESIGN.md (a plan, not built).

The starting point today is the Lists API and the developer portal at /developers (with a quickstart and an interactive reference; docs/API.md), plus the MCP connector that lets an AI agent read and edit your lists (assistant/docs/AGENT-CONNECTOR.md). The API is for your own data, with a personal token. Desk research on who else is in this space, with its unverified claims flagged, is in MARKET.md. Everything below is future work and not built: A bigger developer portal, so other platforms can connect to Arya, with Arya's household data as the shared source. That means more endpoints (receipts, spend, what is running low), webhooks, OAuth sign-in instead of a personal token, SDKs and sample apps. Smart fridges, cooking devices and home robots that add what is empty or expiring to the list and feed back what was used. Online grocery delivery services and apps, to send a list for ordering and to bring back the real receipt and prices. (There is no cart or payment in Arya today; see assistant/docs/SPEC.md, "Not in scope".) Any app that understands a household's food and purchase habits (meal planners, nutrition and budgeting apps), connected through the same API and the import and export below. Every integration would be opt-in, per household, with scoped permissions and a clear way to revoke it.

Richer spend tracking and analysis, with filters (by store, category, person, period, price per unit). The Spending screen exists today; deeper analysis and filters are not built. Export to other budgeting apps (spend and receipts as CSV or a direct connection). Today the API lists your own data (docs/API.md); a budgeting export is not built. Import lists from other list apps (a file or a link). Not built.

All of these are ideas. None is designed or built. Each would need my go-ahead and, where it touches personal data, a privacy review first. Everyday use Meal planning from what is running low and what to use soon, with a shopping list built from the plan. Recipe to shopping list, then to stores. Turn a recipe (link, photo or typed) into list items, then use the household's receipt history to suggest where and which brand to buy. Not built. Budget goals per store or per month on the Spending screen, with a gentle heads-up and never a lock. Barcode scan to add an item or check a price against your own history. Pantry and fridge check-in by photo (outside the current spec). Home Screen widgets and watch glances for the list and for use-soon items. Calendar-aware reminders, such as "you host on Saturday". Voice assistants (Siri, Google Assistant) adding to the list (Alexa is built but switched off, see below), and more connectors beyond the Muse agent and MCP. Receipt import from email or a store account, so no photo is needed. Warranty and return reminders read from receipts (Return Regret already shows returns are tracked). Waste tracking and a monthly "what we threw away" view. Gift and event lists with a shared link and no account needed to view. Accessibility: a screen-reader review and a calmer Quest mode. (Text size and spacing already exist in Settings, under Display.) Community Neighborhood and store pages with shared tips, labelled as opt-in. Verified store news from shoppers, expiring when nobody confirms it. Seasonal Quest events, themed skins (escape room) and household leaderboards that stay private by default. A mapper reputation and thanks for people who map stores, with no pay attached. Clubs and teams (families, roommates, offices, school pantries, food banks). A public gallery of store maps that are fresh and photo-backed. Shared price alerts when a household opts in to share a figure. AI and open weights A hosted open-weights reader for receipts, for people who want that choice. A smaller on-device model for offline add and quick matches. Better product merge and split suggestions in the Curator, and learned substitutions (the usual brand when one is out of stock). Ask Arya acting on more things, with a confirm step for anything that changes data. A public set of evals so others can check the reader scores. Trust, privacy and operating it One place for privacy controls. Export my data and Delete my account already exist in Settings, under Account. The idea is to gather them with the other privacy choices. A public status page and an uptime history. A staging address, and automated CI instead of manual runs. A published API with webhooks and OAuth (docs/API.md, "Later"). Store permission programme for mapping, and a takedown route for stores.

documents.t: Docker with Compose (Docker Desktop, or Docker Engine and the Compose plugin). Nothing else: no Python, no Node. A Meta Model API key for the AI parts: receipts, Ask, photos and voice. Make one at dev.meta.ai (API keys, then Create API key). It starts with LLM_. Without it, lists, the demo household and Quest still run, but anything that reads a photo, answers in Ask or listens to your voice says "This copy of Arya has no Meta key, so AI features are off". A Google Places API key to add stores on your own account. Adding a store searches the Google Places API. Without the key, the store picker says "Google search is not set up" and there is no way to type a store in by hand. The demo household comes with its own stores, so the demo needs no Google key. Everything else is optional. A phone-size window. On a laptop, make the browser about 390 px wide. Camera and microphone steps need a phone, and a phone browser only allows the camera on https. On a phone reaching your computer over plain http:// on your network, use the receipt upload instead of the camera.

Get the code with a shallow clone, which is small and fast. A normal git clone also works and brings the full history (much larger): git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya.git && cd arya Then, from the repository root: cp .env.local.example .env # then put your key on the MODEL_API_KEY line docker compose up --build Open http://localhost:8080. The first build takes a few minutes. On the first visit a "Create your account" sheet opens. That makes the one real account on this copy: a username (lowercase letters, digits and _ % + @ -, and . after the first character) and a password. Use it to snap or upload your own receipts and see them read and saved. That is Arya's core feature. Or tap Close on the sheet and then Try it now for the demo household. The demo keeps nothing. It reads a receipt live on the screen but does not save it. Ask, photos of a list and voice work there with your key. The first start also writes the demo household into a Docker volume. Later starts keep what is there.

To run the live model calls from your own checkout, make a Meta Model API key just for this (dev.meta.ai, API keys, Create API key). Put it on the MODEL_API_KEY line of your local .env. Never commit a filled .env. The MODEL_API_KEY= line in assistant/deploy/.env.example is blank on purpose. The key is sent only to api.meta.ai. Meta keys have no spending cap of their own, so set a usage limit on your Meta billing page, and delete the key at Meta when you are done. Photo receipts: see ARYA_PHOTO_READER below.
documents.s: How do I get a Meta API key?

documents.t: Two matter: MODEL_API_KEY for the AI, and GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY to add stores on your own account. The rest are optional. Setting What it does Default MODEL_API_KEY Your Meta key. Receipts, Ask, photos, voice, notes and store scans use it. Lists, the demo and Quest run without it empty (AI off) ARYA_STORE Where data is kept. json means files in a Docker volume json ARYA_PHOTO_READER auto: Muse Spark reads a photo first, Muse Wonder re-reads one the checks flag. Or spark, wonder auto ARYA_SPARK_TIER Spark runs on Meta's Standard plan standard GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY Needed to add a store on your own account: the store picker searches the Google Places API. Empty means the picker says "Google search is not set up". The demo needs no key empty BASETEN_API_KEY Optional. Muse Spark Open, the staple judge's second seat. Leave empty to skip that check empty ARYA_LOCAL_PORT Use another port if 8080 is taken 8080 Ignore everything else in assistant/deploy/.env.example: Supabase, email, Google, push and the other settings are for the live site. They default off.

Every model call runs on your key and your Meta account. The demo household keeps its visit limit locally too: about $0.40 of live reads per visit and $2 a day for the demo (ARYA_DEMO_SESSION_BUDGET_USD, ARYA_DEMO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD). Pricing is in assistant/docs/MODEL-POLICY.md.

After editing .env, run docker compose up -d. docker compose restart does not re-read .env. Stop: press Ctrl+C, or docker compose down. Your data stays. Start over (wipes the volume; the next start writes the demo household again): docker compose down -v. Another port: set ARYA_LOCAL_PORT in .env.
documents.s: How do I stop it, reset it or change the port?

documents.t: One container, plain http://localhost, no Caddy and no certificate. The session cookie is set to work over plain http (ARYA_INSECURE_COOKIE=1). JSON files in a volume instead of Supabase. No email, so you sign in with the username and password you made on the first visit. Demo Town (the simulated neighborhood, labelled simulated) is on, as on the live demo, and registration is open, so Start my own list on the landing page makes any number of accounts. Groups are on, so two local accounts can share a list. There is no waitlist, no Google sign-in and no email code. The compose.yaml here does not touch the live deploy, which uses assistant/deploy/docker-compose.yml. Next, a step-by-step tour of every feature on your copy: docs/TRY-THE-FEATURES.md.

documents.t: The Tester followed this route step by step from a fresh clone, without a key (the receipt step was not run). The Docker route above was run twice on a Linux server with no Meta key. A cold build (about 55 seconds) from a fresh shallow clone, in a browser at 390x844, worked for start, /health, creating an account, signing in again, the demo, the no-key Ask and receipt messages, and Start shopping. An earlier run with cached build layers, through direct requests, showed that editing .env and the port setting worked. The cold build needed that test machine's proxy certificate added, because its network re-signs HTTPS (see "What if something goes wrong?"). Reading a receipt, photos, voice and a working Ask answer need a real key and were not run on either route. Still untested: a real Meta key, Docker Desktop on a Mac or Windows laptop, and a real phone. You need Python 3.12 or newer (3.13 worked) and Node 22. From the repository root: python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r assistant/api/requirements.txt cd assistant/web && npm ci && npm run build && cd .. ../.venv/bin/python -m harness.make_demo_household data MODEL_API_KEY=<your key> ../.venv/bin/python -m uvicorn api.main:app --port 8000 In MODEL_API_KEY=<your key>, put your key in place of <your key>, or nothing at all for no-key mode (MODEL_API_KEY=). Pasting the angle brackets as they are fails in bash. The snippet leaves your shell in assistant/. Open http://localhost:8000. The address http://localhost:8000/health answers ok when the server is up. These steps were tested on Linux only. macOS and Windows have not been tried. Without a key, Ask shows the "no Meta key" message. On this route its last words, "docker compose up -d", do not apply. Instead, set MODEL_API_KEY and start uvicorn again. To open it from a phone at http://<your computer's IP>:8000, make uvicorn listen on your network address (its --host option) and set ARYA_INSECURE_COOKIE=1 before it. Without that, sign-in may not stick over plain http. I have not tested this on a phone. For front-end work, npm run dev in assistant/web starts Vite.
documents.s: Can I run it without Docker?

documents.t: If you use a coding agent that can run commands on your computer, paste this prompt to it. It uses the no-Docker route, which the Tester followed from a fresh clone (without a key). Read the prompt first. It asks the agent to run commands on your machine. Set up Arya on my computer so I can try it. Repository: https://github.com/vibhortayal/arya 1. Clone the repository into a new, empty folder, cd into it, and open docs/RUN-IT-YOURSELF.md. 2. Follow the section "Can I run it without Docker?" step by step. If something goes wrong, troubleshoot it as you normally would to get Arya running, and use "What if something goes wrong?" in the guide. Do not edit any file that git tracks; the folders the guide's commands create (.venv, node_modules, the web build, the data folder) are expected. 3. Use the no-key demo mode: run the uvicorn command with MODEL_API_KEY= left empty (nothing after the equals sign). Do not ask me for a key, a password or any secret, and do not paste or print one. 4. When the server is up, tell me the local address (http://localhost:8000), that /health answers "ok", and the sign-in steps: tap Close on the "Create your account" sheet, then tap "Try it now" for the demo household. Tell me to make the browser about 390 px wide. Without a key, anything that reads a photo or answers in Ask says "This copy of Arya has no Meta key, so AI features are off". That is expected.

documents.t: "This copy of Arya has no Meta key, so AI features are off. Put your key from dev.meta.ai after MODEL_API_KEY= in the .env file, then run: docker compose up -d" MODEL_API_KEY is empty, or the container was not recreated after you edited .env. Fix .env, then docker compose up -d. Receipts says "Reading paused" and there is no key. The same cause as above: add the key and run docker compose up -d. Port already in use. Set ARYA_LOCAL_PORT to a free port. A model error with a key set. The key was rejected or has no credit. Check it at dev.meta.ai. The build fails to download packages, with a certificate error (pip or npm). A proxy that re-signs HTTPS is the usual cause. Build on a network without one, or add your proxy's certificate to Docker. Docker Hub answers 429 Too Many Requests. The pull limit for your address is used up. Wait a few minutes and run the build again, or run docker login. Status check. http://localhost:8080/health answers when the app is up. This is not the feature "Use your own Meta key" in the live app's Settings, which is unfinished, switched off and not used (see After the hackathon). Here the key is the server's key, set in .env.

The builder wrote these steps and checked them on a local copy (docker compose up --build, http://localhost:8080) on 2026-11-02. "Needs your key" means the step calls a Meta model, so MODEL_API_KEY must be set in .env. Everything else works without a key. Arya is a phone app. For the closest view, use your browser's phone mode (for example 390 × 844), or open the address from a phone on the same network.

documents.t: Copy the settings file and add your key: cp .env.local.example .env, then put your key from dev.meta.ai after MODEL_API_KEY=. Run docker compose up --build, then open http://localhost:8080. A Create your account sheet opens. You can either: Fill in a username and a password, then tap Create account. Use it for section 9, your own receipts. Tap Close, then Try it now to open the demo household (sections 1 to 8). Sign-in on your own copy is a plain username and password (see Run it yourself). To make more accounts, use Start my own list at the bottom of the landing page.

Tap Try it now, then Skip for now (or Show me every screen for the 2-minute tour). The household shops in Demo Town, a simulated neighbourhood of 800 households and 8 stores: Trader Jill's, Safeday, Costcozy, Whole Meadows, Aldo's, Targot, Sprout Street and Corner Market. Anything from the neighbours is marked SIMULATED. Today shows these cards, top to bottom: Next trip: Trader Jill's, 4 items, with "Hummus 10 oz is out here today". Near you today: "Hummus 10 oz is out at Trader Jill's. 3 neighbors reported it… Safeday has it at $4.29" and "Whole Milk 1 gal is cheapest at Aldo's, $3.50". Running low: Whole Milk and Sourdough Loaf, each with how often you buy it. Cheaper elsewhere: "Pasture Eggs: cheaper at Costcozy, $6.03 there, $6.96 at Trader Jill's". Use soon: 6 things from your receipts that can expire. Still good?: one item to check. Spending: October total. Price watch: Sourdough Loaf is 6.6% more than in July.

Tap More, then Stores. My stores lists Costcozy and Trader Jill's (starred), plus Aldo's and Safeday. Each is marked Demo Town (simulated). Tap Find stores to search all stores by name, ZIP or address. Tap More, then Lists, then Trader Jill's. The list opens with a heads-up: "Hummus 10 oz is out. Safeday has it…". Hummus is marked Out here · 3 neighbors. Under Suggested for Trader Jill's, tap an item to see why Arya suggests it, then + Add.

The 3-minute video cannot show everything. This list is the standout parts of Arya that exist today, each with why it matters and where the detail lives. Everything here is built and in the code. Ideas that are not built are on the After the hackathon page. For the product in full, see assistant/docs/SPEC.md and assistant/docs/USER-JOURNEYS.md.

A model reads, code checks. Muse Spark reads a receipt photo first (Wonder is the backup reader). Plain code then checks every line against the printed total before anything posts. Why: a wrong price never goes in silently. assistant/docs/MODEL-POLICY.md, docs/evals/ Returns net out against purchases. "To check" marks lines Arya is unsure about. Fix this line edits the name, quantity and price, with Undo. The printed total never changes. The original photo is kept. Why: you stay in control of your record. Background reading with progress: several receipts at once, and you can leave while Arya reads them.

Patterns from your own receipts: how often you buy each item and what you pay at each store. From that, the list shows what is running low and what to use soon, each with a reason (the "why" sheet). A staple judge with two seats: Muse Spark decides what counts as a staple. Muse Spark Open (open weights, hosted on Baseten) judges again from item names only. Disagreements are kept for review. Why: names advise, purchase facts decide. assistant/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md The Curator proposes product merges and splits with reasons; nothing changes until you apply it. Your own lists, and every item sits on one: you make your own lists, for example, one for each store, such as Trader Jill's or Costcozy. When you add an item, it goes to the list you say, or to your only list, or Arya asks "Which list?". Works offline (signed-in accounts): lists and other screens show as last saved, and list edits queue until you are back online. Receipts, Ask, photos, voice and sharing need a connection. Signed-in accounts keep a cached copy. The demo saves offline list changes for that visit only.

Cheaper store, price trend, similar items per ounce, which store to buy each item at, and the cost of food waste, on a Spending screen. Why: nothing is fetched from store sites, flyers or the web, so every figure is yours. assistant/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md Community prices and live "how busy is the store" are not live; the opt-in records a choice only (SPEC.md, FR-11.7).

A chat over a snapshot of your household's data that can also act on statements such as "we finished the yogurt". Answers in the language you write; Spanish and Hindi were the ones verified (assistant/docs/MULTILINGUAL-ASK.md). Voice dictation and a photo of a handwritten list.

A hunt through a model of your store with no clock and no way to lose. Start shopping on a list opens it at that list's store and ends on your receipt. docs/quest/GAME-DESIGN.md Find it for me: point the camera at a shelf; SAM 3.1 boxes candidates and Muse Spark checks each one. Map my store: a guided camera scan. SAM 3.1 pixelates the people it detects before anything is kept. If that fails, the frame is discarded. Detection is not perfect and is not scored. A store counts as mapped only where it has a usable, fresh photo, so the status is earned. docs/quest/MAP-MY-STORE.md Build a store from three questions, practice in it, and save it.

Groups share lists between the people you live with, joined by a single-use code or an invite link. Receipts stay with whoever filed them. Daily reminders for what is running low. Live on the hosted app. You opt in, and on iPhone the app must be added to the Home Screen first. Add to Home Screen, so it opens like an app. A navigation tab (the bottom buttons) you arrange yourself.

Keeping Arya running (Settings, About Arya) shows your own AI use by kind (receipts and photos, Ask, store maps, lists and voice), this month and since you joined, and the whole app's AI cost and who pays. Why: Arya is free, and the paid AI reading is shown openly. How Arya uses AI says where AI is used and when to double-check, and that Arya is not a food-safety check. Arya's powers lists what Arya does for you now and what turns on as you add receipts. Guards: a daily budget for the real app and a separate one for the demo, a per-visit cap on the demo, and a heads-up and pause for unusually heavy use. assistant/docs/OPS.md

Lists API and developer portal at /developers (quickstart in curl, Python and JavaScript, interactive reference). docs/API.md A connector for your own AI agent (MCP): Make my code, then ask the Muse agent to connect. assistant/docs/AGENT-CONNECTOR.md
